results.title: instrumental variables - Weak first stage in 2SLS - Cross Validated
results.content: # Weak first stage in 2SLS. $Z$ is by construction independent of $N$ and $S$, it is a random, continuous factor that is instrumented in the system. However, I'm concerned that my first stage may be too weak due to the limited impact of $Z$. So are there any checks that I could use to qualify the weakness of my first stage ? asked Dec 3, 2015 at 8:13. 1,30222 gold badges1515 silver badges3232 bronze badges. ## 2 Answers 2. To test for weak instruments you would test the joint significance of your instruments' coefficients via an F-test. The typical rule of thumb is that an F-statistic of more than 10 is fine (see Stock and Yogo, 2002), however, this is not a theorem and people may still give you a hard time if your test statistic is close to 10. In case you only have one instrument, this F-statistic is equivalent to the square of the t-statistic of your instrument's coefficient in the first stage. Should you find that your instrument is weak, i.e. if you get an F-statistic of less than 10 (or close to it), then you can use alternative estimators which are somewhat more robust to this weak instruments problem. "A survey of weak instruments and weak identification in generalized method of moments." Journal of Business & Economic Statistics 20.4 (2002): 518-529. 73.2k88 gold badges117117 silver badges365365 bronze badges. answered Dec 3, 2015 at 10:06. 19.6k2020 gold badges8888 silver badges104104 bronze badges. * $\begingroup$ I have only one instrument; the t-statistic of $\beta\_z$ is $9.63$ in my first stage, so I guess I'm ok. This and other "weak-instrument robust" methods are implemented int he `ivmodel` R package. answered Jan 10, 2020 at 2:34. 12.9k66 gold badges5757 silver badges9292 bronze badges.
